## 8b - the equal-time tie (reviewer finding F46-1)

`endpoint_window` took a candidate only when its `observed_at` was STRICTLY newer, so at an equal
timestamp (the ledger writes `observed_at` without fractional seconds, ties are likely) the first
entry stayed: a 30 % observation could hide a 99 % one and the reviewer stayed available. The
recorded-observation selection and the live-rollout replacement now share ONE comparison
(`quota::window_obs_wins`): newer `observed_at` wins; at an equal instant the higher primary
`used_percent` wins, then the higher secondary (the rule `newer_wins` already applied to rollouts).
Tests: `endpoint_window_at_an_equal_time_keeps_the_fuller_window_in_both_orders` and
`the_live_window_replaces_a_lower_recorded_one_at_an_equal_time` (both failed before the fix).
`observed_at` comparison sites: `quota.rs` recorded selection (fixed), live replacement (fixed),
`newer_wins` (already correct); `health.rs` only consumes `endpoint_window` (n.a.); the machine-wide
record merge has no `observed_at` comparison (n.a.).

Plugin parity: `codex-consult-common.ps1` `Get-EndpointWindow` (lines ~6985 and ~6989) uses
`-gt $best.ObservedAt` for both the recorded and the live selection - the SAME tie. A plugin
TECH_DEBT candidate (not edited here).

## 8c - the equal-time merge per window (reviewer finding F48-1)

The 8b tuple rule (primary first) could hide a blocking weekly window: at an equal `observed_at`,
primary 40 % / secondary 99 % lost to primary 50 % / secondary 20 %. The coordinator's rule: at an
EQUAL `observed_at` the windows merge PER WINDOW - the endpoint's primary is the observation with
the higher primary `used_percent` (with that observation's reset), the secondary independently the
higher secondary (with its reset); a strictly newer `observed_at` still replaces both.
`quota::select_window` (recorded and live selection of `endpoint_window`, replacing
`window_obs_wins`) and `quota::merge_observation` (the sub-agent and account-rollout aggregation,
built on `newer_wins`, which still decides newer-or-not) apply it. Tests:
`endpoint_window_at_an_equal_time_merges_per_window_in_both_orders`,
`the_live_window_merges_per_window_with_a_crossing_recorded_one` (both assignments),
`merge_observation_keeps_each_fuller_window_at_an_equal_instant`; the 8b tests stay.
The plugin's T17 fix of the tie (see 8b) must use the same per-window rule.

## 8d - a total order for tied windows (reviewer finding F50-1)

At an equal `observed_at` and an equal `used_percent` the per-window pick kept the FIRST window's
reset, so a null or past reset could hide a future one by ordering. One comparator
(`quota::cmp_window_rank`, used by `select_window` for the recorded and live selections and by
`merge_observation`) now ranks two observations of the same window at the comparison time `now`:
(1) a known FUTURE reset beats a known PAST reset beats a missing (null) one; (2) the higher
`used_percent`; (3) the later `resets_at`; (4) identical - either. A strictly newer `observed_at`
still replaces both windows. Tests: `equal_shares_rank_by_the_reset_in_every_order`,
`the_live_window_ranks_a_future_reset_over_a_null_one_at_a_tie`,
`a_past_reset_never_hides_a_future_one_whatever_the_share`,
`the_tie_selection_is_the_same_for_every_permutation` (4 observations, all 24 orders).
The plugin's T17 fix must use this full ordering (future > past > null, then share, then later reset).

## 8e - one comparison instant, finite percentages (reviewer findings F52-1, F52-2)

The 8d rank depends on `now`, and each comparison sampled the clock on its own, so a reset crossing
from future to past DURING one aggregation (the rollout reads happen between merges) made the pick
order-dependent (A=(100 %, R), B=(99 %, S), C=(30 %, S), R < S). `now` is now sampled ONCE at the
top of each public entry point - `endpoint_window` (-> `endpoint_window_at`), `account_window`
(-> `account_window_at`), `codex_run_quota` - and passed as a parameter to `select_window`,
`merge_observation` and `cmp_window_rank` (no clock read inside the comparator); the health
evaluation hands the same `now_utc` to `endpoint_window_at` and to the "reset in the past" verdict.
F52-2: `finite_percent` treats a non-finite or out-of-range (outside 0..=100) share - a "NaN" /
"inf" text included - as an ABSENT window, in the window states (the block evaluation), the
selection and the rollout parser; the comparator uses `f64::total_cmp`. Tests:
`one_comparison_instant_makes_the_aggregation_order_independent` (A/B/C, all 6 orders, an instant
before R keeps A, one between R and S keeps B, both block),
`a_non_finite_percent_never_hides_a_valid_block`,
`the_tie_selection_is_the_same_for_every_order_of_six` (720 orders, a past reset and a NaN included).
The plugin's T17 fix needs the same single instant and the finite check.

## 8f - the account cache keeps raw observations, newer invalid windows do not replace (F55-1, F55-2)

F55-1: `account_window` cached only the WINNER picked at an earlier instant and returned it for 60 s,
so after that winner's reset a discarded equal-time observation that still blocked was lost. The
cache (per codex home) now holds the RAW observations of the account's rollouts
(`read_account_observations`); `account_window_at` runs the selection (`merge_observation`) at
every lookup with the requested `now`, the 60 s TTL only bounds how often the rollouts are read.
F55-2 (fail closed, per window): an observation with no VALID window is absent; a strictly newer
observation replaces a window only where its own window is valid, otherwise the older valid window
of that kind stays, and an older observation fills only the kinds the newer one lacks - in
`select_window` (recorded and live) and in `merge_observation`; at an equal instant the 8d rank
decides. Tests: `the_account_cache_selects_at_each_requested_instant`,
`a_newer_invalid_record_keeps_the_older_valid_window` (NaN / out of range, both orders, plus the
newer-partial case), and the permutation test now runs 5040 orders of seven observations (a
NaN-only newer record included). The tests that read `endpoint_window` are serialised with those
that switch the process-wide live source on (a flake of the shared global). The plugin's T17 fix
needs the same cache shape and the per-window validation.

## 8g - every window carries its OWN observation instant (reviewer finding F58-1)

Partial-window aggregation kept an older observation's window but stamped the aggregate with the
NEWER observation's instant, so a later comparison treated the retained window as newer than it
was: with t1 < t2 < t3, A = primary 30 % at t1, B = secondary 10 % at t3, C = primary 99 % at t2,
the fold A, B, C kept 30 % (B had promoted A's primary to t3) and A, C, B kept 99 %. Now
`Observation` carries `primary_at` / `secondary_at` (`window_at(kind)`: its own, else `at`),
`EndpointWindow` and `AccountWindow` carry `window_at: [primary, secondary]`, and a candidate window
is compared only with the instant of THAT retained window (strictly newer replaces, equal takes the
8d rank, older is kept; an invalid window has no instant and never replaces). The aggregate
`observed_at` / `at` is derived (the latest per-window instant) for display and the age of the
record, never for a replacement decision. The instants flow: rollout parse (`at` of the event) ->
`merge_observation` (per-window instants kept) -> `account_window_at` (`AccountWindow.window_at`
from the aggregate, over the raw cache) -> `endpoint_window_at` (recorded candidates carry their
entry instant on both windows, the live candidate its `window_at`) -> `select_window` (compares per
window with `EndpointWindow.window_at`). Tests: `partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_in_the_recorded_selection`,
`partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_in_merge_observation`,
`partial_windows_keep_their_own_instants_across_the_recorded_live_split`,
`distinct_instant_partial_windows_are_order_independent` (720 orders, distinct instants, partial
windows, a NaN-only one). The plugin's T17 fix needs per-window timestamps too.

## 8h - the per-window instants survive persistence (reviewer finding F60-1, supersedes F58-1)

8g kept each window's instant in memory, but `Observation::to_quota` wrote ONE aggregate
`observed_at`, so a recorded aggregate (the ledger's `quota`, the machine-wide health record - both
carry the quota object verbatim) lost the provenance: `endpoint_window_at` rebuilt both instants
from it, and an aggregate of A (primary 30 at t1) and B (secondary 10 at t3) labelled its primary
with t3 and beat C (primary 99 at t2). The quota record now carries two optional keys after
`observed_at`: `primary_observed_at` and `secondary_observed_at` (ISO, local offset), written by
`to_quota` only for a window that is present (a null quota keeps exactly `primary, secondary,
observed_at`). They are written wherever the quota is written (the ledger entry of a codex run, the
machine-wide record) and read by the recorded selection in `endpoint_window_at`; the aggregate
`observed_at` is only the LEGACY fallback of a record written before 8h (keys absent), and the
selected `EndpointWindow.quota` is re-stamped with them. Plugin compatibility: the oracle reads
only keys it knows; its one strict key check is on the NULL quota (`primary,secondary,observed_at`),
which is unchanged. Tests: `the_quota_record_carries_per_window_instants_through_ledger_and_health`,
`a_persisted_aggregate_cannot_promote_its_older_window` (both recorded orders and C live),
`a_legacy_record_without_window_instants_uses_the_aggregate_instant`. The plugin's T17 fix needs
the same two ledger fields.

## 8i - lossless instants, the imprecise rule, the legacy policy (reviewer finding F62-1)

8h stored each window's instant through a seconds-only formatter, so a recorded 99 % observed at
12:00:00.900 read back as 12:00:00 and an OLDER live 30 % at 12:00:00.100 looked strictly newer and
replaced it. Three rules now:
1. **Lossless**: `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` are written as RFC3339 with the
   fractional seconds the instant has (`2026-10-13T12:00:00.900+00:00`; no fraction when it has none),
   in `to_quota` and in the re-stamp of `select_window`; read back exactly. The aggregate
   `observed_at` keeps its seconds-only format (compat).
2. **Imprecise compare** (`cmp_instants`): an instant without a fractional part is imprecise (a legacy
   aggregate, a second-precision record, a whole-second rollout stamp). If either side is, the two
   are compared at whole-second granularity: a recency win needs a strictly later whole second, the
   same second is a tie and the 8d rank decides (future reset > past > null, higher share, later
   reset). Both precise: exact. (A precise instant that happens to be exactly on a second reads as
   imprecise - the conservative side.)
3. **Legacy records** (no per-window keys): the window instants are UNKNOWN (`EndpointWindow.
   window_legacy`; the aggregate stands in only for the legacy-vs-legacy comparison). A legacy window
   never wins on recency against a window with a known instant - that pair is decided by the 8d rank
   alone; no per-window key is written for a legacy window.
Tests: `a_subsecond_instant_survives_the_record_and_beats_an_older_live_one`,
`a_second_precision_record_ties_with_a_live_instant_of_the_same_second`,
`a_legacy_record_never_wins_on_recency_against_a_known_instant` (replaces the 8h legacy test; the
health verdict sees the block). Pairwise comparisons mixing precise and imprecise instants are not
strictly transitive across three or more observations within one second; the rank keeps each pair
deterministic. The plugin's T17 fix needs the same three rules.

## 8j - ONE total order per window (supersedes the 8i pairwise precision rule)

The 8i rule (whole-second compare only when a side is imprecise) was not transitive across mixed
precisions inside one second, and a legacy window decided by rank against known ones broke the fold
the same way. Now every instant comparison in the selection and the merge is made at WHOLE-SECOND
granularity (`cmp_instants`: floor to the second; fractions are never an ordering key): a strictly
later second wins on recency; the same second is a tie that `cmp_window_rank` (8d) decides. The
fractional instants stay stored, re-stamped and round-tripped exactly (8i) - bookkeeping, not a
key. Within one kind of window (known instants, or legacy aggregates compared at the same
granularity) (floor second, rank) is a lexicographic total order. The legacy rule stays - an unknown
instant never wins on recency against a known one, the rank alone decides - and to keep the fold
order-independent `select_window` keeps the best KNOWN and the best LEGACY candidate per window
(`EndpointWindow` slots) and resolves the visible window from that pair (the legacy one only if it
outranks the known one by the rank), so the pick is a function of the candidate SET. Inside one
second the higher-usage window wins: the conservative side (usage only rises within a window; a
reset is already ranked by future/past). Tests: `whole_second_order_is_transitive_for_the_abc_precision_case`
(a imprecise :00 50 %, b :00.100 99 %, c :00.900 30 %, six orders -> 99 %),
`mixed_precision_candidates_give_one_pick_in_every_order` (six candidates - two imprecise, two with
fractions in one second, one in the next second, one legacy, partial windows - 720 orders through
the recorded selection and `merge_observation`, plus a recorded/live split); the 8i sub-second test
now passes by rank (99 % at :00.900 against live 30 % at :00.100). The plugin's T17 fix uses the
same total order.

## Planned after the tag: worker telemetry (the operator's request, 2026-10-13 22:40)

Goal: know which worker tier (opus / sonnet / haiku / other) did what kind of work and how it ended, across installs
(users on an Opus-max or a Sonnet-max plan), WITHOUT spending the coordinator's tokens. Design:
- The signal source is the host's hook, not the model: Claude Code runs `SubagentStop` (and `SubagentStart`) hooks
  as shell commands with a JSON on stdin (session, transcript paths, the agent id - to verify: `agent_transcript_path`).
  C3 ships `c3 hook subagent-stop`; the plugin ships the PowerShell mirror in its hooks.json. Zero model tokens.
- From the subagent's transcript the hook computes CLASSES AND NUMBERS only: tier (the plugin's agent names
  opus-worker/sonnet-worker/haiku-worker, else `other`), the actual model (closed list of published names, else
  `other`), outcome (`completed`, `error:rate_limit`, `error:context` (prompt too long), `error:other`, `stopped`),
  duration bucket, input/output token buckets, tool-use count bucket, tool-error count bucket, edits bucket
  (Edit/Write calls -> `read-only` vs `writes`), whether a verification command ran (cargo test / pytest / run-all
  patterns -> `verified`), resumes (SendMessage continuations of the same agent). Never a prompt, a path, a name.
- Optional judgment at ~50 tokens: `c3 worker rate <agent id> yes|partly|no --note` (mirrors `-Rate` for reviewers);
  the event carries the mark like the reviewer rating (`rating_rev`, judge).
- One event per subagent end to the intake (event class `worker`); the intake (xelth.com crates/telemetry) gets the
  schema and a public table "workers": per tier x outcome counts, error share, median duration/tokens, the rating
  share - so a user can see whether e.g. sonnet-worker finishes verification waves as often as opus-worker.
- Cost: hook CPU only; the rating is optional. Privacy as the existing contract (closed classes, consult_ref-style
  pseudonymous keys). Order: after v0.2.0 - C3 wave "worker telemetry", the plugin mirror, the intake + page.

The brief bundles one safe decision with two unsafe ones. Extending the closed vocabulary is nearly free: `classes.rs` already maps anything unknown to `other`/`unknown`, so new values never break old intakes. The risky parts are (a) committing to a *published score* before the denominators are comparable, and (b) assuming the hook can see effort.

Options the brief does not list:

- **(5) Tier-split panels as the experiment.** Alternative 2 (local A/B) is dismissed as "nothing learned for other users" — but the routed panel already exists. Send the same brief at two efforts to two seats of one panel; the existing consult events capture it for everyone once `effort` ships. This is alternative 1 and 2 combined, at panel cost.
- **(6) Publish counts, keep scores local.** `c3 scoreboard` is already local. Ship only `effort` on events and let each install compute its own usefulness-per-cost; the intake publishes distributions, not rankings. Defers the irreversible "published metric" decision until the findings join (alternative 3) exists.
- **(7) Record effort now, commit to no score at all.** Schema first, semantics later.

What I would need to choose: does z.ai expose more than three glm-5.3 tiers; does `SubagentStop` stdin (or the transcript metadata) carry the Agent call's effort override; how is the intake schema versioned today.

## Q1 — tiers and denominator

Tiers: gpt-6-astra (window-bound): chore low, checkpoint/reading medium, diff-review/acceptance high, core-contract/stuck xhigh. glm-5.3 (money-bound, no 5-hour window): chore low, everything else high, stuck max — the asymmetry is real and the policy should encode it. Denominator: findings-confirmed per unit of the *binding constraint* — window-share for OpenAI, money for GLM, wall time only as a guard. Finding F1: window share is not a cross-vendor denominator (quota.rs reads Codex rollouts only), so "usefulness per window share" cannot be the single published score. Design not listed: score the **marginal finding** — findings no other panel seat produced — per cost unit; it survives routed panels where seats differ.

## Q2 — worker capture

`SubagentStop` is the right capture point for Claude Code; other hosts report via the coordinator's own `rate` path with tier `other`. Must stay out: transcript/cwd/repo paths, session id (hash it), the agent label as typed. Effort: do not trust the transcript — the coordinator knows effort at spawn; have it write a local worker-id→{tier,effort} registry the hook reads (zero tokens, no parsing). Attribution under rework: add outcome `reworked`, marked at rating time; credit completion to the last worker, charge the rework against the original tier's score. Without this the original tier's completion share is inflated (F5).

## Q3 — add to the vocabulary now

`effort` (sent, closed none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max), `effort_requested` (preset name or `other`), `effort_native` (pre-mapping label — otherwise medium→high is indistinguishable from native high later, F2), `cost_basis` (window|money|none) so denominators stay interpretable, and `schema_v` per event. Worker event: tier, effort, outcome class, duration/token buckets, verified flag, resume count, reworked flag.

Missing options include deterministic scouting, local aggregation before upload, and randomized shadow evaluations that leave production routing unchanged. Choosing requires the task mix, tolerated misses, latency target, binding subscription limits, and coordinator rework cost.

**Q1.** Initial experimental defaults—not measured optima:

| Purpose | Astra | GLM-5.3 |
|---|---|---|
| Chore/extraction | low | low |
| Reading/checkpoint | medium | high |
| Framing/decision | high | high |
| Diff-review/acceptance | high | max |
| Core-contract/stuck | xhigh | max |

Treat reading as a stage, not another purpose. Escalate on unresolved evidence or risk, not just the purpose label. [Z.ai documents](https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3) exactly three tiers. [OpenAI documents](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra) Astra `max` too; that does not establish support through this bridge’s subscription route.

There is no universal denominator. Confirmed findings are benefits, not costs. Compare independently verified task quality against quota consumption, elapsed time, paid usage/points, and rework separately. Within an isolated subscription experiment, use total quality benefit divided by total attributable quota consumption, including failed attempts; track both windows. Current quota snapshots are not attributable consumption (finding #1). Deduplicate confirmed findings and measure misses on known-defect cases; `implemented` alone is not confirmation. Randomize paired trials by task class and report uncertainty and rating coverage.

**Q2.** Use command hooks at Start and Stop, plus reconciliation for missing endings; define an execution episode separately from a resumed worker. Current [hook documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-input-fields) includes conditional `effort.level`, but Stop lacks a model field. Validate the installed host and resolve actual model identity locally; retain unknown effort instead of dropping workers.

Upload only reconstructed allowlisted classes/counts. Exclude raw hook JSON, prompts, messages, transcripts, paths, commands, errors, agent names, session/thread/agent IDs, credentials, and notes. Mint random worker references; keep their mapping local. Apply existing telemetry opt-out and deletion behavior. Other hosts can submit the same adapter-neutral record with explicit provenance and missingness.

Rate worker contribution separately from final wave success: accepted unchanged, minor rework, substantial rework, discarded, or unknown; record rework duration and independent verification separately. Command execution does not prove verification passed.

**Q3.** Promise versioned compatibility, not a vocabulary frozen forever. Add schema/capability/policy versions; requested and sent effort separately; confirmation state; policy source; resolved model class; work class/stage; measurement source/completeness; cost basis and attribution quality. Keep `none`, `unknown`, and `unsupported` distinct. Worker records need random reference, episode/revision, lifecycle outcome, duration/token buckets, rework class, verification result, and rating revision/judge. Copy effort metadata from the original run when rating. Aggregate finding outcomes locally against existing `consult_ref`; private finding IDs need not leave the machine.

**Q4.** No digest cap guarantees honesty. Start at 1,000 tokens containing evidence pointers, invariants, hypotheses, omissions, and uncertainty. Give the judge the original brief, diff inventory, and direct source access; require independent inspection of relevant boundaries. Budget exhaustion means incomplete coverage, never automatic acceptance. Compare digest-assisted review against independent review.

- **RC2:** In a disposable checkout, run eight frozen known-defect cases at two efforts in randomized order with isolated account usage and blind adjudication. Permission: workspace-write. # Handoff 01 - claude: framing panel A - measuring reviewers and workers (usage tiers, worker telemetry)

Date: 2026-10-14. Base commit: C3 `v0.2.1` (8a133f8); the PowerShell plugin `claude-codex-consult` 0.6.1 (main
dcb9d59, wave 30 unreleased). Both are the same program: a bridge that lets a coordinating agent (Claude Code, Codex
CLI and other hosts) consult reviewer models through their CLIs, with a reviewer roster, a findings store, and an
anonymised telemetry intake at `xelth.com/T/`. Read `README.md` and `docs/port/wave8-quota.md` of this repository
for the current behaviour; the roster shape is in the README's "Reviewer roster and panel".

## Question

Before any of this is implemented, we want the panel's angle on two measurement designs that will shape the
roster, the telemetry schema and the routing for a long time: (A) usage TIERS for the two standing consultants
(OpenAI gpt-6-astra through the ChatGPT subscription, Zhipu glm-5.3 through z.ai) - which reasoning effort to
send for which purpose, and how to score a tier; (B) WORKER telemetry - the coordinator's own sub-agents (Claude
Code tiers haiku / sonnet / opus / fable AND their effort levels) counted and scored at near-zero token cost so the
tier choice can be improved from data. Both change a closed telemetry vocabulary that is hard to change once
published.

## Task state

- Done: the telemetry intake (consult and rating events; engine, vendor class, a closed list of model names, purpose,
  outcome class, counts - never a task, prompt, path or name); the quota windows (wave 8: the 5-hour and weekly
  ChatGPT windows read from the Codex rollouts; a round of review costs 8-23 % of the 5-hour window at effort high;
  a forked thread with sub-agents once cost 96 % in 186 s); effort vocabularies per endpoint (caps-v1: openai
  low|medium|high|xhigh; z.ai low|high|max with medium->high and xhigh->max); purpose presets (chore low, checkpoint
  medium, acceptance high, core-contract/stuck xhigh); the ratings (`rate`, `useful yes|partly|no`) per
  consultation; a routed panel seats reviewers by track record.
- Open: no telemetry event carries the effort; no event exists for workers at all; the roster has no per-purpose
  effort policy per entry; nothing measures a tier against its cost.
- Not in scope: new reviewer engines; the browser engine; the intake's hosting.

## Evidence

- `crates/c3/src/telemetry/classes.rs` - the closed vocabulary of the events (what can be added without breaking
  the published schema).
- `crates/c3-core/src/quota.rs` - what a run costs in window share and tokens (`tokens`, `quota`, `budget` in the
  ledger entry): the cost side of a score exists per consultation already.
- `.collab/parity-0.6.1-2026-10-08/state.md`, sections "Planned (2026-10-14 10:40): usage tiers" and "Planned
  after the tag: worker telemetry" - the coordinator's current sketch (below).
- Observed today: nine review rounds of one wave with gpt-6-astra at effort high found one real defect each
  (F46-1 .. F62-1), 183-234 s and 10-15 % of the 5-hour window per round; a GLM round at `max` is cheaper in money
  and has no 5-hour window; Claude Code workers (opus / sonnet) did each fix in 15-70 minutes.

## The coordinator's sketch (to be challenged)

(A) Usage tiers. Roster entries get an effort POLICY per purpose (e.g. gpt-6-astra: chore medium, reading pass
medium, diff-review high, core-contract xhigh; glm-5.3: chore low, review high, stuck max). The consult and
rating events carry `effort` (the tier SENT after the vocabulary mapping - closed: none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max)
and `effort_requested` (the preset name). The intake's usefulness table splits per reviewer x effort. Routing
"scout and judge": a cheap tier (GLM low, or a Haiku worker) reads the diff and writes a digest handoff; the judge
(Astra high, or GLM max) gets the digest plus a call cap; the digest survives a cold cache. Open: does z.ai expose
more than three tiers on glm-5.3; is `medium` on gpt-6-astra good enough for a reading pass; how to SCORE a tier -
usefulness per 5-hour-window share, not per run.

(B) Worker telemetry. Claude Code's `SubagentStop` hook (the plugin can ship it) fires at each worker's end with
the agent type; the bridge records one closed-class event per worker: tier (haiku|sonnet|opus|fable|other), effort
level if the host exposes it, duration class, outcome class (reported | stopped-by-coordinator | error | unknown),
and a coordinator-side mark after the fact (`c3 workers rate <id> useful yes|partly|no`) - never the brief, the
files or the repository. The intake gets a "workers" table (counts, error share, usefulness per tier x effort).
Cost: one hook invocation per worker, no model tokens. Open: can the hook see the effort and the tier reliably
(agent definition vs model alias); how to attribute a wave's success to a worker when the coordinator reworked it;
what a user of another host (Codex CLI agents, Kimi) can report.

## Alternatives weighed

1. **Effort policy in the roster + effort in the events (the sketch)** - small schema change now; the score needs
   months of data.
2. **No new telemetry; a local experiment first** (the coordinator runs the same brief at two efforts for a week and
   compares findings per window share) - no schema risk; nothing learned for other users.
3. **Score reviewers by findings confirmed, not by usefulness marks** - more objective (a finding later marked
   `implemented`/`verified` is a hit); needs the findings store joined to the events (ids are private today).
4. **Workers: no hook, the coordinator's own notes in STATE.md** - zero code; not comparable across users.

Current preference: 1 for reviewers with the window-share denominator; 3 as the long-term score once the findings
join exists; for workers the hook with closed classes, but only if the effort is visible to it.

## Questions

- **Q1.** For (A): which effort tiers would you send per purpose for gpt-6-astra and glm-5.3, and what is the right
  denominator to score a tier (window share, money, wall time, findings confirmed)? Name a design we did not list.
- **Q2.** For (B): is the SubagentStop hook the right capture point; what MUST stay out of the event for privacy;
  and how would you attribute a worker's result when the coordinator reworks it?
- **Q3.** The schema: which fields would you add to the closed vocabulary now so we never have to break it later?
- **Q4.** The "scout and judge" routing: where does it fail (a digest that hides the defect), and what cap on the
  scout's output keeps the judge honest?

Answer by number. Keep it under 600 words.

# Handoff 01 - claude: framing panel A - measuring reviewers and workers (usage tiers, worker telemetry)

Date: 2026-10-14. Base commit: C3 `v0.2.1` (8a133f8); the PowerShell plugin `claude-codex-consult` 0.6.1 (main
dcb9d59, wave 30 unreleased). Both are the same program: a bridge that lets a coordinating agent (Claude Code, Codex
CLI and other hosts) consult reviewer models through their CLIs, with a reviewer roster, a findings store, and an
anonymised telemetry intake at `xelth.com/T/`. Read `README.md` and `docs/port/wave8-quota.md` of this repository
for the current behaviour; the roster shape is in the README's "Reviewer roster and panel".

## Question

Before any of this is implemented, we want the panel's angle on two measurement designs that will shape the
roster, the telemetry schema and the routing for a long time: (A) usage TIERS for the two standing consultants
(OpenAI gpt-6-astra through the ChatGPT subscription, Zhipu glm-5.3 through z.ai) - which reasoning effort to
send for which purpose, and how to score a tier; (B) WORKER telemetry - the coordinator's own sub-agents (Claude
Code tiers haiku / sonnet / opus / fable AND their effort levels) counted and scored at near-zero token cost so the
tier choice can be improved from data. Both change a closed telemetry vocabulary that is hard to change once
published.

## Task state

- Done: the telemetry intake (consult and rating events; engine, vendor class, a closed list of model names, purpose,
  outcome class, counts - never a task, prompt, path or name); the quota windows (wave 8: the 5-hour and weekly
  ChatGPT windows read from the Codex rollouts; a round of review costs 8-23 % of the 5-hour window at effort high;
  a forked thread with sub-agents once cost 96 % in 186 s); effort vocabularies per endpoint (caps-v1: openai
  low|medium|high|xhigh; z.ai low|high|max with medium->high and xhigh->max); purpose presets (chore low, checkpoint
  medium, acceptance high, core-contract/stuck xhigh); the ratings (`rate`, `useful yes|partly|no`) per
  consultation; a routed panel seats reviewers by track record.
- Open: no telemetry event carries the effort; no event exists for workers at all; the roster has no per-purpose
  effort policy per entry; nothing measures a tier against its cost.
- Not in scope: new reviewer engines; the browser engine; the intake's hosting.

## Evidence

- `crates/c3/src/telemetry/classes.rs` - the closed vocabulary of the events (what can be added without breaking
  the published schema).
- `crates/c3-core/src/quota.rs` - what a run costs in window share and tokens (`tokens`, `quota`, `budget` in the
  ledger entry): the cost side of a score exists per consultation already.
- `.collab/parity-0.6.1-2026-10-08/state.md`, sections "Planned (2026-10-14 10:40): usage tiers" and "Planned
  after the tag: worker telemetry" - the coordinator's current sketch (below).
- Observed today: nine review rounds of one wave with gpt-6-astra at effort high found one real defect each
  (F46-1 .. F62-1), 183-234 s and 10-15 % of the 5-hour window per round; a GLM round at `max` is cheaper in money
  and has no 5-hour window; Claude Code workers (opus / sonnet) did each fix in 15-70 minutes.

## The coordinator's sketch (to be challenged)

(A) Usage tiers. Roster entries get an effort POLICY per purpose (e.g. gpt-6-astra: chore medium, reading pass
medium, diff-review high, core-contract xhigh; glm-5.3: chore low, review high, stuck max). The consult and
rating events carry `effort` (the tier SENT after the vocabulary mapping - closed: none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max)
and `effort_requested` (the preset name). The intake's usefulness table splits per reviewer x effort. Routing
"scout and judge": a cheap tier (GLM low, or a Haiku worker) reads the diff and writes a digest handoff; the judge
(Astra high, or GLM max) gets the digest plus a call cap; the digest survives a cold cache. Open: does z.ai expose
more than three tiers on glm-5.3; is `medium` on gpt-6-astra good enough for a reading pass; how to SCORE a tier -
usefulness per 5-hour-window share, not per run.

(B) Worker telemetry. Claude Code's `SubagentStop` hook (the plugin can ship it) fires at each worker's end with
the agent type; the bridge records one closed-class event per worker: tier (haiku|sonnet|opus|fable|other), effort
level if the host exposes it, duration class, outcome class (reported | stopped-by-coordinator | error | unknown),
and a coordinator-side mark after the fact (`c3 workers rate <id> useful yes|partly|no`) - never the brief, the
files or the repository. The intake gets a "workers" table (counts, error share, usefulness per tier x effort).
Cost: one hook invocation per worker, no model tokens. Open: can the hook see the effort and the tier reliably
(agent definition vs model alias); how to attribute a wave's success to a worker when the coordinator reworked it;
what a user of another host (Codex CLI agents, Kimi) can report.

## Alternatives weighed

1. **Effort policy in the roster + effort in the events (the sketch)** - small schema change now; the score needs
   months of data.
2. **No new telemetry; a local experiment first** (the coordinator runs the same brief at two efforts for a week and
   compares findings per window share) - no schema risk; nothing learned for other users.
3. **Score reviewers by findings confirmed, not by usefulness marks** - more objective (a finding later marked
   `implemented`/`verified` is a hit); needs the findings store joined to the events (ids are private today).
4. **Workers: no hook, the coordinator's own notes in STATE.md** - zero code; not comparable across users.

Current preference: 1 for reviewers with the window-share denominator; 3 as the long-term score once the findings
join exists; for workers the hook with closed classes, but only if the effort is visible to it.

## Questions

- **Q1.** For (A): which effort tiers would you send per purpose for gpt-6-astra and glm-5.3, and what is the right
  denominator to score a tier (window share, money, wall time, findings confirmed)? Name a design we did not list.
- **Q2.** For (B): is the SubagentStop hook the right capture point; what MUST stay out of the event for privacy;
  and how would you attribute a worker's result when the coordinator reworks it?
- **Q3.** The schema: which fields would you add to the closed vocabulary now so we never have to break it later?
- **Q4.** The "scout and judge" routing: where does it fail (a digest that hides the defect), and what cap on the
  scout's output keeps the judge honest?

209	    }

211	    /// The ledger's `quota` `{primary, secondary, observed_at}` (observed_at local), then - only for
212	    /// a window that is present - `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at`: the instant
213	    /// each retained window was OBSERVED (wave 8h; `observed_at` is the derived aggregate, the
214	    /// legacy fallback of a record written without them).
215	    pub fn to_quota(&self) -> Value {
216	        let mut q = json!({
217	            "primary": self.primary.as_ref().map(Window::to_json),
218	            "secondary": self.secondary.as_ref().map(Window::to_json),
219	            "observed_at": self.at.map(|a| iso(to_local(a))),
220	        });
221	        for (kind, key) in WINDOW_AT_KEYS.iter().enumerate() {
222	            let present = if kind == 0 {
223	                self.primary.is_some()
224	            } else {
225	                self.secondary.is_some()
226	            };
227	            if let (true, Some(t)) = (present, self.window_at(kind)) {
228	                q[*key] = Value::String(iso_instant(to_local(t)));
229	            }
230	        }
231	        q
232	    }
233	}

247	    last_input: Option<i64>,

259	/// Every `token_count` event of a rollout text, in file order.
260	fn token_events(text: &str) -> Vec<TokenEvent> {
261	    let mut out = Vec::new();
262	    for line in text.split('\n') {
263	        if !line.contains("\"token_count\"") {
264	            continue;
265	        }
266	        let v: Value = match serde_json::from_str(line.trim()) {
267	            Ok(v) => v,
268	            Err(_) => continue,
269	        };
270	        let payload = if v.get("payload").map(|p| p.is_object()).unwrap_or(false) {
271	            &v["payload"]
272	        } else {
273	            &v
274	        };
275	        if payload.get("type").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) != Some("token_count") {
276	            continue;
277	        }
278	        let at = v
279	            .get("timestamp")
280	            .and_then(|t| t.as_str())
281	            .and_then(|t| DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(t).ok());
282	        let info = &payload["info"];
283	        let tt = &info["total_token_usage"];
284	        let (total, total_key) = if tt.is_object() {
285	            (
286	                Some(Totals {
287	                    input: num(&tt["input_tokens"]),
288	                    cached: num(&tt["cached_input_tokens"]),
289	                    output: num(&tt["output_tokens"]),
290	                }),
291	                Some(tt.clone()),
292	            )
293	        } else {
294	            (None, None)
295	        };
296	        let last_input = num(&info["last_token_usage"]["input_tokens"]);
297	        let context_window = num(&info["model_context_window"]);
298	        let rl = &payload["rate_limits"];
299	        let has_limits = rl.is_object();
300	        let (limit_id, primary, secondary) = if has_limits {
301	            (
302	                rl["limit_id"].as_str().unwrap_or("").to_string(),
303	                window_of(&rl["primary"]),
304	                window_of(&rl["secondary"]),
305	            )
306	        } else {
307	            (String::new(), None, None)
308	        };
309	        out.push(TokenEvent {
310	            at,
311	            total,
312	            total_key,
313	            last_input,
314	            context_window,
315	            has_limits,
316	            limit_id,
317	            primary,
318	            secondary,
319	        });
320	    }
321	    out
322	}

326	/// `Read-RolloutText`: the whole file (at most 64 MiB - its end), or its last `tail_bytes`; a cut
327	/// start drops the first, partial line. `""` when unreadable.
328	fn read_rollout_text(path: &Path, tail_bytes: u64) -> String {
329	    let mut f = match std::fs::File::open(path) {
330	        Ok(f) => f,
331	        Err(_) => return String::new(),
332	    };
333	    let len = match f.metadata() {
334	        Ok(m) => m.len(),
335	        Err(_) => return String::new(),
336	    };
337	    let mut take = len;
338	    if tail_bytes > 0 && take > tail_bytes {
339	        take = tail_bytes;
340	    }
341	    if take > ROLLOUT_MAX_BYTES {
342	        take = ROLLOUT_MAX_BYTES;
343	    }
344	    let start = len - take;
345	    if f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(start)).is_err() {
346	        return String::new();
347	    }
348	    let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(take as usize);
349	    if f.take(take).read_to_end(&mut buf).is_err() {
350	        return String::new();
351	    }
352	    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf).into_owned();
353	    if start > 0 {
354	        match text.find('\n') {
355	            Some(i) => text[i + 1..].to_string(),
356	            None => String::new(),
357	        }
358	    } else {
359	        text
360	    }
361	}

363	/// `Read-RolloutHead`: the first line (its `session_meta`), at most 64 KiB of it. `""` when
364	/// unreadable.
365	pub fn read_rollout_head(path: &Path) -> String {
366	    let f = match std::fs::File::open(path) {
367	        Ok(f) => f,
368	        Err(_) => return String::new(),
369	    };
370	    let mut buf = Vec::new();
371	    if f.take(ROLLOUT_HEAD_BYTES).read_to_end(&mut buf).is_err() {
372	        return String::new();
373	    }
374	    let end = buf.iter().position(|b| *b == b'\n').unwrap_or(buf.len());
375	    String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..end]).into_owned()
376	}

378	/// What one rollout says (`Get-RolloutUsage`).
379	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
380	pub struct RolloutUsage {
381	    pub found: bool,
382	    pub path: PathBuf,
383	    pub bytes: u64,
384	    /// The LAST `token_count` that names a window, else the last one that carries `rate_limits`.
385	    pub window: Option<Observation>,
386	    /// The last running total.
387	    pub total: Option<Totals>,
388	    /// The last total before `before` (`None` when none or without `before`).
389	    pub baseline: Option<Totals>,
390	    /// The `token_count` events at or after `before` (all without it) whose total differs from the
391	    /// event before: one per model request.
392	    pub calls: i64,
393	    /// The largest per-call input among them.
394	    pub max_input: Option<i64>,
395	    /// The last `model_context_window`.
396	    pub context_window: Option<i64>,
397	}

399	/// `Get-RolloutUsage`: `tail_bytes` > 0 reads only the end of the file (the budget watch; the
400	/// baseline and the calls then cover only that end).
401	pub fn rollout_usage(
402	    path: &Path,
403	    before: Option<DateTime<FixedOffset>>,
404	    tail_bytes: u64,
405	) -> RolloutUsage {
406	    let mut r = RolloutUsage {
407	        path: path.to_path_buf(),
408	        ..Default::default()
409	    };
410	    if path.as_os_str().is_empty() || !path.is_file() {
411	        return r;
412	    }
413	    r.found = true;
414	    r.bytes = std::fs::metadata(path).map(|m| m.len()).unwrap_or(0);
415	    let mut prev_total: Option<Value> = None;
416	    let mut last_limits: Option<Observation> = None;
417	    for ev in token_events(&read_rollout_text(path, tail_bytes)) {
418	        let in_run = match before {
419	            None => true,
420	            Some(b) => ev.at.map(|a| a >= b).unwrap_or(false),
421	        };
422	        if let Some(t) = ev.total {
423	            r.total = Some(t);
424	            if let (Some(b), Some(a)) = (before, ev.at) {
425	                if a < b {
426	                    r.baseline = Some(t);
427	                }
428	            }
429	            if in_run && ev.total_key != prev_total {
430	                r.calls += 1;
431	                if let Some(li) = ev.last_input {
432	                    if r.max_input.map(|m| li > m).unwrap_or(true) {
433	                        r.max_input = Some(li);
434	                    }
435	                }
436	            }
437	            prev_total = ev.total_key.clone();
438	        }
439	        if ev.context_window.is_some() {
440	            r.context_window = ev.context_window;
441	        }
442	        if ev.has_limits {
443	            let w = Observation {
444	                primary: ev.primary,
445	                secondary: ev.secondary,
446	                at: ev.at,
447	                primary_at: None,
448	                secondary_at: None,
449	                limit_id: ev.limit_id,
450	            };
451	            if w.named() {
452	                r.window = Some(w.clone());
453	            }
454	            last_limits = Some(w);
455	        }
456	    }
457	    if r.window.is_none() {
458	        r.window = last_limits;
459	    }
460	    r
461	}

479	/// `Get-UuidV7Time`: the creation time of a UUIDv7 (its first 48 bits, unix milliseconds); `None`
480	/// for another version.
481	pub fn uuid_v7_time(id: &str) -> Option<DateTime<Utc>> {
482	    let b = id.as_bytes();
483	    if !is_uuid(id) || b[14] != b'7' {
484	        return None;
485	    }

491	/// `Get-LocalDayDirs`: the `<root>/<yyyy>/<MM>/<dd>` directories of the LOCAL days from `from` to
492	/// `to` (at most 7 plus the last day).
493	pub fn local_day_dirs(root: &Path, from: NaiveDate, to: NaiveDate) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
494	    let (mut a, mut b) = (from, to);
495	    if b < a {
496	        std::mem::swap(&mut a, &mut b);
497	    }
498	    let mut days: Vec<NaiveDate> = Vec::new();
499	    let mut d = a;
500	    while d <= b && days.len() < 7 {
501	        days.push(d);
502	        d = match d.succ_opt() {
503	            Some(n) => n,
504	            None => break,
505	        };
506	    }
507	    if days.last() != Some(&b) {
508	        days.push(b);
509	    }
510	    days.iter()
511	        .map(|d| {
512	            root.join(format!("{:04}", d.year()))
513	                .join(format!("{:02}", d.month()))
514	                .join(format!("{:02}", d.day()))
515	        })
516	        .collect()
517	}

523	/// The `rollout-*.jsonl` files of a directory whose name ends with `<suffix>` (lower case
524	/// compared), with their write times.
525	fn rollouts_in(dir: &Path, suffix: Option<&str>, out: &mut Vec<(SystemTime, PathBuf)>) {
526	    let rd = match std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
527	        Ok(rd) => rd,
528	        Err(_) => return,
529	    };
530	    for e in rd.flatten() {
531	        let name = e.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_lowercase();
532	        if !(name.starts_with("rollout-") && name.ends_with(".jsonl")) {
533	            continue;
534	        }
535	        if let Some(s) = suffix {
536	            if !name.ends_with(s) {
537	                continue;
538	            }
539	        }
540	        let meta = match e.metadata() {
541	            Ok(m) if m.is_file() => m,
542	            _ => continue,
543	        };
544	        out.push((meta.modified().unwrap_or(SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH), e.path()));
545	    }
546	}

548	fn rollouts_recursive(dir: &Path, suffix: &str, out: &mut Vec<(SystemTime, PathBuf)>, depth: u32) {
549	    if depth > 6 {
550	        return;
551	    }
552	    rollouts_in(dir, Some(suffix), out);
553	    if let Ok(rd) = std::fs::read_dir(dir) {
554	        for e in rd.flatten() {
555	            if e.file_type().map(|t| t.is_dir()).unwrap_or(false) {
556	                rollouts_recursive(&e.path(), suffix, out, depth + 1);
557	            }
558	        }
559	    }
560	}

562	/// `Get-CodexRolloutPath`: the newest `<codex home>/sessions/**/rollout-*-<id>.jsonl`, `None` when
563	/// there is none. A UUIDv7 id carries its creation time: that local day and the days around it are
564	/// looked at first, then the whole tree.
565	pub fn codex_rollout_path(thread: &str, codex_home: &str) -> Option<PathBuf> {
566	    if !is_uuid(thread) || codex_home.is_empty() {
567	        return None;
568	    }
569	    let root = Path::new(codex_home).join("sessions");
570	    if !root.is_dir() {
571	        return None;
572	    }
573	    let suffix = format!("-{}.jsonl", thread.to_lowercase());
574	    let mut found: Vec<(SystemTime, PathBuf)> = Vec::new();
575	    if let Some(created) = uuid_v7_time(thread) {
576	        let day = local_date(created);
577	        let from = day.pred_opt().unwrap_or(day);
578	        let to = day.succ_opt().unwrap_or(day);
579	        for d in local_day_dirs(&root, from, to) {
580	            rollouts_in(&d, Some(&suffix), &mut found);
581	        }
582	    }
583	    if found.is_empty() {
584	        rollouts_recursive(&root, &suffix, &mut found, 0);
585	    }
586	    found.sort_by_key(|(t, _)| std::cmp::Reverse(*t));
587	    found.into_iter().next().map(|(_, p)| p)
588	}

600	/// `Get-CodexSubagentRollouts`: the rollouts of the local days from `since` to now, written since
601	/// then (5 s slack), whose first line names the thread - or one of its sub-agents, recursively - as
602	/// `parent_thread_id`.
603	pub fn subagent_rollouts(parent: &str, since: DateTime<Utc>, codex_home: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
604	    if parent.is_empty() || codex_home.is_empty() {
605	        return Vec::new();
606	    }
607	    let root = Path::new(codex_home).join("sessions");
608	    if !root.is_dir() {
609	        return Vec::new();
610	    }
611	    let mut files: Vec<(SystemTime, PathBuf)> = Vec::new();
612	    for d in local_day_dirs(&root, local_date(since), local_date(Utc::now())) {
613	        rollouts_in(&d, None, &mut files);
614	    }
615	    let cut: SystemTime = (since - Duration::seconds(5)).into();
616	    let name_re = regex::Regex::new(&format!(r"({})\.jsonl$", uuid_re().as_str())).unwrap();
617	    let mut parent_of: Vec<(PathBuf, String, String)> = Vec::new();
618	    for (_, p) in files.into_iter().filter(|(t, _)| *t >= cut) {
619	        let name = p
620	            .file_name()
621	            .map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string())
622	            .unwrap_or_default();
623	        let id = match name_re.captures(&name) {
624	            Some(c) => c[1].to_lowercase(),
625	            None => continue,
626	        };
627	        let head = read_rollout_head(&p);
628	        if let Some(c) = parent_re().captures(&head) {
629	            parent_of.push((p, c[1].to_lowercase(), id));
630	        }
631	    }
632	    parent_of.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
633	    let mut parents: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
634	    parents.insert(parent.to_lowercase());
635	    let mut out: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
636	    let mut changed = true;
637	    while changed {
638	        changed = false;
639	        for (p, par, id) in &parent_of {
640	            if out.contains(p) || !parents.contains(par) {
641	                continue;
642	            }
643	            out.push(p.clone());
644	            parents.insert(id.clone());
645	            changed = true;
646	        }
647	    }
648	    out
649	}

651	/// `Select-NewerWindow`: `true` when `b` wins over `a` - the newer one that names a window; at the
652	/// same instant the one whose fullest window is fuller (the threads of one account report at the
653	/// same moment, and some report a stale share: the highest is the account's).
654	pub fn newer_wins(a: Option<&Observation>, b: Option<&Observation>) -> bool {
655	    let named = |w: Option<&Observation>| w.map(|w| w.named()).unwrap_or(false);
656	    let (bw, b_at) = match b {
657	        Some(bw) if named(b) && bw.at.is_some() => (bw, bw.at.unwrap()),
658	        _ => return false,
659	    };
660	    let (aw, a_at) = match a {
661	        Some(aw) if named(a) && aw.at.is_some() => (aw, aw.at.unwrap()),
662	        _ => return true,
663	    };
664	    if b_at > a_at {
665	        return true;
666	    }
667	    if b_at < a_at {
668	        return false;
669	    }
670	    bw.fullest() > aw.fullest()
671	}

673	/// A used share as the quota records it (a number or a numeric text): `None` - the window is ABSENT
674	/// - for a non-finite (`NaN`, `inf`) or out-of-range (outside 0..=100) value.
675	pub fn finite_percent(v: &Value) -> Option<f64> {
676	    let f = match v {
677	        Value::Number(n) => n.as_f64()?,
678	        Value::String(s) => s.trim().parse::<f64>().ok()?,
679	        _ => return None,
680	    };
681	    (f.is_finite() && (0.0..=100.0).contains(&f)).then_some(f)
682	}
683	
684	/// The TOTAL, order-independent ranking of two observations of the SAME window at an equal
685	/// instant, evaluated at `now`: (1) a known future reset beats a known past reset beats a missing
686	/// one (a past reset means the window is reset, whatever its share); (2) the higher
687	/// `used_percent`; (3) the later `resets_at`; (4) identical - either. `Greater` when `a` ranks
688	/// above `b`.
689	fn cmp_window_rank(
690	    a: (f64, Option<DateTime<FixedOffset>>),
691	    b: (f64, Option<DateTime<FixedOffset>>),
692	    now: DateTime<Utc>,
693	) -> std::cmp::Ordering {
694	    let rank = |r: Option<DateTime<FixedOffset>>| match r {
695	        Some(t) if t.with_timezone(&Utc) > now => 2u8,
696	        Some(_) => 1,
697	        None => 0,
698	    };
699	    rank(a.1)
700	        .cmp(&rank(b.1))
701	        .then(a.0.clamp(0.0, 100.0).total_cmp(&b.0.clamp(0.0, 100.0)))
702	        .then(a.1.cmp(&b.1))
703	}
704	
705	/// The observation the thread/sub-agent/account aggregation keeps after seeing `b`: PER WINDOW,
706	/// a candidate window is compared with the instant of THAT retained window - strictly newer
707	/// replaces, an equal instant takes the total [`cmp_window_rank`] at `now`, older is kept; a window
708	/// the candidate lacks (or an invalid one) never replaces. Each kept window carries its own
709	/// instant; `at` of the result is derived (the latest of them), for display only.
710	pub fn merge_observation(
711	    a: Option<Observation>,
712	    b: Option<&Observation>,
713	    now: DateTime<Utc>,
714	) -> Option<Observation> {
715	    // an observation that names no (valid) window or has no instant is absent
716	    let usable = |o: &Observation| o.named() && o.at.is_some();
717	    let (av, bv) = match (a.as_ref().filter(|o| usable(o)), b.filter(|o| usable(o))) {
718	        (Some(av), Some(bv)) => (av, bv),
719	        (None, Some(bv)) => return Some(bv.clone()),
720	        _ => return a,
721	    };
722	    let key = |w: &Window| {
723	        (
724	            w.used_percent,
725	            w.resets_at
726	                .as_deref()
727	                .and_then(|r| DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(r).ok()),
728	        )
729	    };
730	    let mut wins: [Option<Window>; 2] = [None, None];
731	    let mut ats: [Option<DateTime<FixedOffset>>; 2] = [None, None];
732	    for kind in 0..2 {
733	        let win = |o: &Observation| {
734	            if kind == 0 {
735	                o.primary.clone()
736	            } else {
737	                o.secondary.clone()
738	            }
739	        };
740	        let (aw, bw) = (win(av), win(bv));
741	        let (a_at, b_at) = (av.window_at(kind), bv.window_at(kind));
742	        let take_b = match (&aw, &bw) {
743	            (_, None) => false,
744	            (None, Some(_)) => true,
745	            (Some(x), Some(y)) => match match (b_at, a_at) {
746	                (Some(bt), Some(at)) => cmp_instants(bt, at),
747	                (b_t, a_t) => b_t.cmp(&a_t),
748	            } {
749	                std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => true,
750	                std::cmp::Ordering::Less => false,
751	                std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
752	                    cmp_window_rank(key(y), key(x), now) == std::cmp::Ordering::Greater
753	                }
754	            },
755	        };
756	        if take_b {
757	            wins[kind] = bw;
758	            ats[kind] = b_at;
759	        } else {
760	            wins[kind] = aw;
761	            ats[kind] = a_at;
762	        }
763	    }
764	    let [primary, secondary] = wins;
765	    let [primary_at, secondary_at] = ats;
766	    let at = [(&primary, primary_at), (&secondary, secondary_at)]
767	        .into_iter()
768	        .filter(|(w, _)| w.is_some())
769	        .filter_map(|(_, t)| t)
770	        .max();
771	    let newest = if bv.at > av.at { bv } else { av };
772	    Some(Observation {
773	        primary,
774	        secondary,
775	        at,
776	        primary_at,
777	        secondary_at,
778	        limit_id: newest.limit_id.clone(),

794	/// `Get-CodexRunQuota`: the rollout of the run's thread and the sub-agent rollouts of that thread
795	/// written during the run. `baseline_thread`: the thread whose running total before the run is
796	/// subtracted - the parent of a fork, the thread itself on a resume, `""` for a new thread.
797	pub fn codex_run_quota(
798	    thread: &str,
799	    started_at: DateTime<Utc>,
800	    baseline_thread: &str,
801	    codex_home: &str,
802	) -> RunQuota {
803	    // ONE comparison instant for the whole aggregation (the rollout reads happen between merges)
804	    let now = Utc::now();
805	    let mut r = RunQuota {
806	        quota: null_quota(),
807	        tokens: None,
808	        path: None,
809	        bytes: 0,
810	    };
811	    if thread.is_empty() {
812	        return r;
813	    }
814	    let path = match codex_rollout_path(thread, codex_home) {
815	        Some(p) => p,
816	        None => return r,
817	    };
818	    let before = Some(started_at.fixed_offset());
819	    let u = rollout_usage(&path, before, 0);
820	    r.path = Some(path);
821	    r.bytes = u.bytes;
822	    let base = if !baseline_thread.is_empty() && baseline_thread.eq_ignore_ascii_case(thread) {
823	        u.baseline
824	    } else if !baseline_thread.is_empty() {
825	        codex_rollout_path(baseline_thread, codex_home)
826	            .and_then(|pp| rollout_usage(&pp, before, 0).baseline)
827	    } else {
828	        None
829	    };
830	    let mut win = u.window.clone();
831	    let (mut sub_count, mut sub_input, mut sub_calls) = (0i64, 0i64, 0i64);
832	    for sp in subagent_rollouts(thread, started_at, codex_home) {
833	        let su = rollout_usage(&sp, None, 0);
834	        sub_count += 1;
835	        sub_calls += su.calls;
836	        if let Some(i) = su.total.and_then(|t| t.input) {
837	            sub_input += i;
838	        }
839	        win = merge_observation(win, su.window.as_ref(), now);
840	    }
841	    if let Some(w) = &win {
842	        r.quota = w.to_quota();
843	    }
844	    let minus = |a: Option<i64>, b: Option<i64>| -> Option<i64> {
845	        match (a, b) {
846	            (None, _) => None,
847	            (Some(a), None) => Some(a),
848	            (Some(a), Some(b)) => Some((a - b).max(0)),
849	        }
850	    };
851	    let t = u.total;
852	    let bt = |f: fn(&Totals) -> Option<i64>| base.as_ref().and_then(f);
853	    r.tokens = Some(json!({
854	        "input": t.and_then(|t| minus(t.input, bt(|b| b.input))),
855	        "cached": t.and_then(|t| minus(t.cached, bt(|b| b.cached))),
856	        "output": t.and_then(|t| minus(t.output, bt(|b| b.output))),
857	        "thread_input": t.and_then(|t| t.input),
858	        "calls": u.calls,
859	        "max_input": u.max_input,
860	        "context_window": u.context_window,
861	        "subagents": { "count": sub_count, "input": sub_input, "calls": sub_calls },
862	    }));
863	    r
864	}

937	    }

939	        let w = &quota[key];
940	        if !w.is_object() {

948	            w["window_minutes"]
949	                .as_str()
950	                .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse().ok())
951	        });

971	/// reset lies in the past `5h reset (last 96% until 18:32)`; `""` when the quota names no window.
972	pub fn format_windows(quota: &Value, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> String {

1104	    };

1120	                b.secondary.as_ref().and(b.window_at(1)),

1185	/// The ONE selection of the endpoint window (recorded and live): a candidate strictly newer than
1186	/// `best` replaces it; at an EQUAL `observed_at` (the ledger serialises without fractions, so ties
1187	/// happen) the windows merge PER WINDOW - the higher primary `used_percent` keeps its own reset,
1188	/// and independently the higher secondary - so a blocking weekly window is never hidden behind a
1189	/// fuller 5-hour one. `source` of the result is the candidate's when it contributed a window.
1190	fn select_window(
1191	    best: Option<EndpointWindow>,
1192	    cand_at: [Option<DateTime<FixedOffset>>; 2],
1193	    cand_legacy: [bool; 2],
1194	    quota: &Value,
1195	    source: &'static str,
1196	    fingerprint: String,
1197	    now: DateTime<Utc>,
1198	) -> Option<EndpointWindow> {
1199	    const KEYS: [&str; 2] = ["primary", "secondary"];
1200	    // a window is VALID with a finite share AND an instant; an invalid one never replaces
1201	    let cand_valid = |k: usize| quota_used(quota, KEYS[k]).is_some() && cand_at[k].is_some();
1202	    if !cand_valid(0) && !cand_valid(1) {
1203	        return best;
1204	    }
1205	    // the total order WITHIN one kind of window: (floor second of the instant, then the 8d rank)
1206	    let key = |w: &Value| {
1207	        (
1208	            finite_percent(&w["used_percent"]).unwrap_or(0.0),
1209	            when_offset(&w["resets_at"]),
1210	        )
1211	    };
1212	    let beats = |c: &WindowSlot, cur: &WindowSlot| match cmp_instants(c.at, cur.at) {
1213	        std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => true,
1214	        std::cmp::Ordering::Less => false,
1215	        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
1216	            cmp_window_rank(key(&c.win), key(&cur.win), now) == std::cmp::Ordering::Greater
1217	        }
1218	    };
1219	    let first = best.is_none();
1220	    let mut out = best.unwrap_or_else(|| EndpointWindow {
1221	        quota: json!({"primary": null, "secondary": null, "observed_at": quota["observed_at"].clone()}),
1222	        observed_at: cand_at[0].or(cand_at[1]).unwrap_or_else(now_offset_fixed),
1223	        window_at: [None, None],
1224	        window_legacy: [false, false],
1225	        slots: [[None, None], [None, None]],
1226	        source,
1227	        fingerprint: fingerprint.clone(),
1228	    });
1229	    let prev_observed = out.observed_at;
1230	    let mut took = false;
1231	    for k in 0..2 {
1232	        if !cand_valid(k) {
1233	            continue;
1234	        }
1235	        let Some(at) = cand_at[k] else { continue };
1236	        let cand = WindowSlot {
1237	            win: quota[KEYS[k]].clone(),
1238	            at,
1239	        };
1240	        let kind = usize::from(cand_legacy[k]);
1241	        let replace = match &out.slots[kind][k] {
1242	            None => true,
1243	            Some(cur) => beats(&cand, cur),
1244	        };
1245	        if replace {
1246	            out.slots[kind][k] = Some(cand.clone());
1247	        }
1248	        // resolve the visible window: the best known one, unless the best legacy one outranks it
1249	        // by the 8d rank alone (an unknown instant never wins on recency against a known one)
1250	        let (known, legacy) = (&out.slots[0][k], &out.slots[1][k]);
1251	        let (win, at, is_legacy) = match (known, legacy) {
1252	            (Some(kn), Some(lg)) => {
1253	                if cmp_window_rank(key(&lg.win), key(&kn.win), now) == std::cmp::Ordering::Greater {
1254	                    (lg.win.clone(), lg.at, true)
1255	                } else {
1256	                    (kn.win.clone(), kn.at, false)
1257	                }
1258	            }
1259	            (Some(kn), None) => (kn.win.clone(), kn.at, false),
1260	            (None, Some(lg)) => (lg.win.clone(), lg.at, true),
1261	            (None, None) => continue,
1262	        };
1263	        if replace && win == cand.win && at == cand.at && is_legacy == cand_legacy[k] {
1264	            took = true;
1265	        }
1266	        out.quota[KEYS[k]] = win;
1267	        out.window_at[k] = Some(at);
1268	        out.window_legacy[k] = is_legacy;
1269	    }
1270	    if let Some(l) = out.window_at.iter().flatten().max().copied() {

1309	/// `when`, orders them) and - when the live source is on and the set holds the built-in openai
1310	/// endpoint - the newest rollout of the codex home ([`account_window`]).

1313	    fp_set: &[&str],

1319	/// [`endpoint_window`] at ONE comparison instant `now` - the instant of every comparison of the
1320	/// selection and (the caller's) "reset in the past" verdict.
1321	pub fn endpoint_window_at(
1322	    consults: &[Value],
1323	    fp_set: &[&str],
1324	    builtin_fingerprint: &str,
1325	    now: DateTime<Utc>,
1326	) -> Option<EndpointWindow> {
1327	    let mut best: Option<EndpointWindow> = None;
1328	    for c in consults {
1329	        let q = &c["quota"];
1330	        if !q.is_object() || (q["primary"].is_null() && q["secondary"].is_null()) {
1331	            continue;
1332	        }
1333	        let rev = &c["reviewer"];
1334	        let fp = if rev.is_null() {
1335	            builtin_fingerprint.to_string()
1336	        } else {
1337	            rev["provider_fingerprint"]
1338	                .as_str()
1339	                .unwrap_or("")
1340	                .to_string()
1341	        };
1342	        if fp.is_empty() || !fp_set.contains(&fp.as_str()) {
1343	            continue;
1344	        }
1345	        // the aggregate instant is the LEGACY fallback (a record written before wave 8h)
1346	        let legacy = when_offset(&q["observed_at"])
1347	            .or_else(|| when_offset(&c["finished_at"]))
1348	            .or_else(|| when_offset(&c["when"]));
1349	        let own = [
1350	            when_offset(&q[WINDOW_AT_KEYS[0]]),
1351	            when_offset(&q[WINDOW_AT_KEYS[1]]),
1352	        ];
1353	        let ats = [own[0].or(legacy), own[1].or(legacy)];
1354	        if ats[0].is_none() && ats[1].is_none() {
1355	            continue;
1356	        }
1357	        let unknown = [own[0].is_none(), own[1].is_none()];
1358	        best = select_window(best, ats, unknown, q, "recorded", fp, now);
1359	    }
1360	    if fp_set.contains(&builtin_fingerprint) {
1361	        if let Some(home) = live_codex_home() {
1362	            if let Some(live) = account_window_at(&home, now) {
1363	                best = select_window(
1364	                    best,
1365	                    live.window_at,
1366	                    [false, false],
1367	                    &live.quota,
1368	                    "rollout",
1369	                    builtin_fingerprint.to_string(),
1370	                    now,
1371	                );
1372	            }
1373	        }
1374	    }
1375	    best
1376	}

1498	            percent: QUOTA_BUDGET_DEFAULT,
1499	            source: "default".into(),
1500	        });
1501	    }
1502	    match raw.parse::<i64>() {
1503	        Ok(v) if (0..=100).contains(&v) => Ok(Budget {
1504	            percent: v,
1505	            source: "CODEX_CONSULT_QUOTA_BUDGET".into(),
1506	        }),
1507	        _ => Err(format!(
1508	            "CODEX_CONSULT_QUOTA_BUDGET must be 0 (off) or a share of the 5-hour window from 1 to 100 percent (got '{raw}')."

1538	/// `Get-ForkReplayGuard`: the parent thread's rollout is replayed on EVERY tool call of a codex fork
1539	/// or resume. A rollout that cannot be found is neither refused nor warned about. `max_kb_env`: the
1540	/// raw `CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB`.
1541	pub fn fork_replay_guard(thread: &str, codex_home: &str, max_kb_env: Option<&str>) -> ForkGuard {
1542	    let mut g = ForkGuard {
1543	        max_kb: FORK_MAX_KB_DEFAULT,
1544	        ..Default::default()
1545	    };
1546	    let raw = max_kb_env.map(str::trim).unwrap_or("");
1547	    if !raw.is_empty() {
1548	        match raw.parse::<i32>() {
1549	            Ok(v) if v >= 0 => g.max_kb = v as i64,
1550	            _ => {
1551	                g.problem = format!(
1552	                    "CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB='{raw}' is not a number of KB (0 = no limit) - the default 512 applies"
1553	                )
1554	            }
1555	        }
1556	    }
1557	    if thread.is_empty() {
1558	        return g;
1559	    }
1560	    let path = match codex_rollout_path(thread, codex_home) {
1561	        Some(p) => p,
1562	        None => return g,
1563	    };
1564	    g.bytes = match std::fs::metadata(&path) {
1565	        Ok(m) => m.len(),
1566	        Err(_) => {
1567	            g.path = Some(path);
1568	            return g;
1569	        }
1570	    };
1571	    g.path = Some(path);
1572	    g.kb = round_even(g.bytes as f64 / 1024.0);
1573	    let tokens_k = round_even(g.kb as f64 / 4.0);
1574	    let what = format!(
1575	        "the parent thread {thread} replays {} KB (~{tokens_k} k tokens) on EVERY tool call of the run",
1576	        g.kb
1577	    );
1578	    if g.max_kb > 0 && g.kb > g.max_kb {
1579	        g.over_limit = true;
1580	        g.refusal = format!(
1581	            "{what}: use -Mode new, or raise CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB (now {})",
1582	            g.max_kb
1583	        );
1584	    } else if g.kb >= FORK_WARN_KB {
1585	        let lim = if g.max_kb > 0 {
1586	            g.max_kb.to_string()
1587	        } else {
1588	            "off".into()
1589	        };
1590	        g.warning = format!(
1591	            "{what} (CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB {lim}); -Mode new starts without that replay"
1592	        );
1593	    }
1594	    g
1595	}
