.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs\24-claudecode-panel-b-watch-browser-zai-claude.md:51:- **F24-2** [major] `crates/c3/src/consult/detached.rs:274`, `crates/c3/src/consult/detach.rs:1105` - A watch that answers 'did anything change since <instant>' from file writes/mtimes alone reports 'nothing' for a detached background that was killed with its status stuck at `running` - only the pid-liveness judgement derives `died` - and for a worker that dies without writing anything; the watch must run the same judgement over open runs, not diff timestamps. Trigger: Kill -9 a detached background (or a host crash while one runs) and then run an mtime-based watch: it says 'nothing since T' while `--status` judges the run died. Evidence: read-code: judgement() imports and uses pid_alive; the judgement states include `died`, computed at read time from pid + start time + host, not from any file write.; read-code: judge() re-derives the state on every query; nothing rewrites the status file when the background dies out-of-band.; inferred: A worker dying with the host emits no stop event at all - the same class of silent loss for worker state files. Verify: RC2: kill a detached background out-of-band and compare an mtime-only scan with `c3 consult --task <t> --status`. Remedy: The watch folds detached runs through judge() (a state flip running→died counts as 'changed'), and worker death is covered by the event journal of finding #3 plus a periodic liveness check on recorded pids.
.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs\24-claudecode-panel-b-watch-browser-zai-claude.md:52:- **F24-3** [note] `crates/c3/src/consult/detach.rs:60` - An unlisted, cheaper mechanism exists: a single append-only, closed-vocabulary event journal (one line per state change: sequence number, kind, instant) that every c3 writer (write_status, the health journal, ledger appends) also appends to; the watch then answers 'since <seq>' exactly, with no mtime heuristics, and a host Monitor has one file to watch instead of a directory tree. Trigger: Building the watch on per-file mtime/`updated` comparisons and then needing cross-file ordering, debouncing and silent-death handling anyway. Evidence: read-code: write_status is the single atomic choke point every detached-state change already flows through - one journal append there covers all detached events.; inferred: The machine health file is a second machine-wide writer that could append the same journal, unifying the watch's inputs. Verify: Prototype one journal append in write_status and a `--since <seq>` read; confirm the watch answer for a scripted start/finish/die sequence matches `--status` exactly. Remedy: Adopt the journal as the watch's source of truth (mtimes become a fallback), keeping the vocabulary closed and local.
.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs\24-claudecode-panel-b-watch-browser-zai-claude.md:53:- **F24-4** [major] `.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs/02-claude-watch-and-browser-engine.md:58`, `.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs/02-claude-watch-and-browser-engine.md:72` - Under preference B' the DOM bridge protocol becomes the real host API: if the 'dumb' extension exposes generic DOM operations (query, click, read text), any catalogued adapter can drive any tab and any site, so the deny-by-default ruling must scope bridge operations per adapter (a capability token bound to the run and an origin allowlist per catalogue entry), not only the WASM-facing API inside C3. Trigger: A catalogued adapter granted read+compose issuing bridge calls against a tab or origin outside its vendor scope (e.g. driving a logged-in unrelated site through the same relay). Evidence: read-code: The sketch puts the deny-by-default host API around the adapter's calls and prefers 'the extension as a dumb, signed DOM bridge' - nothing constrains what the bridge itself will execute.; inferred: A content-script bridge with tab access is privileged exactly to the degree its message protocol allows; the protocol is the capability surface the adapter actually sees. Verify: Write the bridge message spec and walk each operation: does every op name its capability and its allowed origin, and is a call without a matching per-run token refused by the extension? Remedy: Carry a per-adapter, per-run capability token on every bridge message; the extension refuses ops outside the token's scope and the catalogue entry's origin allowlist.
.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs\24-claudecode-panel-b-watch-browser-zai-claude.md:54:- **F24-5** [major] `.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs/02-claude-watch-and-browser-engine.md:59`, `crates/c3/src/engines/codex.rs:9` - Draft-only mode breaks the engine contract's retry semantics: denial retry, format repair and timeout continuation are all re-sends of the prompt, each of which in draft mode requires the user to press send again, and stall/budget timers that keep running while the run awaits the user will turn every slow human into a timeout. Trigger: A draft-mode browser reply that fails output-schema validation with format_retry > 1, or a user who takes ten minutes to press send while the stall cut is armed. Evidence: read-code: The engine adapter's documented flow includes denial retry, format repair (a secondary turn) and timeout continuation - all additional turns of the same subject.; read-code: The stall cut and budget are wall-clock timers over a live process; there is no notion of pausing for an external actor.; inferred: Nothing in the sketch distinguishes 'engine is working' from 'waiting for the user's hands'. Verify: RC5: once a draft round exists, run one with a schema-invalid reply and format_retry 2 and observe whether the retry waits on the user and whether a timer fires meanwhile. Remedy: Add an `awaiting-user-send` state that suspends stall/budget clocks; retries in draft mode are recorded as needing-user rather than silently re-queued; a terminal `user-never-sent` class with an age.
.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs\24-claudecode-panel-b-watch-browser-zai-claude.md:55:- **F24-6** [major] `.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs/02-claude-watch-and-browser-engine.md:56` - The trust boundary of the extension and relay is unspecified: the signed catalogue pins adapters, but the extension - which relays briefs (repository content) and holds the per-run token - has no pinning or update control, and the loopback WebSocket is connectable by any local process, token entropy and binding unstated. Trigger: A browser-store auto-update replaces the audited bridge between two runs, or a local process connects to the loopback port and impersonates the extension (or reads the drafted brief). Evidence: read-code: The rulings cover a signed hash/pointer catalogue of adapters and 'a per-run token' for the relay; nothing covers the extension's own integrity or the relay's admission policy.; inferred: An unpacked/dev-mode extension is editable in place; a store-distributed one updates outside the operator's control - either way the 'tiny and auditable' property is not enforced by anything. Verify: RC3/RC4: read the prior art's manifest to see its distribution form, and attempt an unauthenticated connect to a prototyped loopback relay. Remedy: Pin the extension's build hash in the private plugin's config and refuse a mismatched extension at run start; token of at least 128 bits bound to the run id, exactly one accepted connection per run, briefs sent only after the pin check.
.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs\24-claudecode-panel-b-watch-browser-zai-claude.md:56:- **F24-7** [major] `.collab/consilium-2026-10-14/handoffs/02-claude-watch-and-browser-engine.md:55`, `crates/c3/src/engines/subprocess.rs:59` - The recovery chain's 'no kill without a record' presumes a killable process tree; the browser engine has none - its stop is an abandon of a stream owned by the user's tab - and the sketch names no persisted run record or terminal classes for it, so a crash of C3 or the relay would leave a prepared draft with no trace and no way for a restarted session to find it. Trigger: `--kick` or a budget stop of a browser member, or a C3 crash while a draft sits composed in the user's tab. Evidence: read-code: The existing chain is KillEvent::Before (record the tree before stopping anything) then After - semantics defined entirely over a process tree.; read-code: Detached runs already have the persisted crash-safe record pattern (`starting`/`running`/`done` with budget and members) a browser run record can copy.; inferred: It says 'the same contract ... transcript, kill record' without defining what a kill is when there is no child process. Remedy: A per-member persisted record with states prepared → awaiting-user-send → streaming → done | abandoned | timeout | tab-gone; abandon recorded BEFORE the relay stops (mirroring KillEvent::Before), tab left open by default (closing it is its own capability and record), partial reply salvaged; pending drafts surfaced in the SessionStart phrase.

   46: ## The coordinator's sketch (to be challenged)
   47: 
   48: (A) `c3 watch --task <t> --since <instant> [--worker-state <path>...]`: reads the status files of detached runs,
   49: the tails of the named worker STATE files, the ledger's newest entry and the health journal, and prints ONE line:
   50: `nothing since <instant> (next known event: <detached run budget end / quota reset>)` or `changed: <what>` - exit
   51: code 0 nothing, 3 changed. The host's wake then runs this command first (a few hundred tokens) and reads the context
   52: only on exit 3; a Monitor on the status directory can replace the periodic wake entirely where the host has one. A
   53: `--next` hint lets the coordinator schedule the next wake at the earliest known event instead of a fixed period.
   54: 
   55: (B) An engine `browser` with the same contract as the others (brief in, structured reply out, transcript, kill
   56: record): C3 starts a local relay (WebSocket, loopback only, a per-run token), the Chrome extension connects, an

   61: the output schema like the others; the usefulness table keys on adapter + vendor.
   62: 
   63: ## Alternatives weighed
   64: 
   65: 1. **(A) the watch command + `--next` hint (the sketch)** - small; the host still has to fire the wake.
   66: 2. **(A) a long-lived `c3 serve` that pushes events** (a local socket the host's Monitor can read) - no wasted

{"schema_version":"1","reply_markdown":"## Framing
A is an event-semantics problem, not a file-diff utility; B is a human-owned interactive channel, not another autonomous subprocess. Fix those contracts before choosing transport.

**Q1.** Fold a monotonic, append-only, closed-vocabulary event journal plus the existing detached judgement: status/member transitions, liveness-derived `died`, unreadable records, and foreign-host runs as `unknown`, never as quiet. Use `--since <sequence>`, not a wall-clock instant. Do not fold worker STATE prose.

The cheapest reliable schedule is `min(cache-TTL ceiling, periodic liveness deadline, real operator/run deadline)`, with jitter; budget end and quota reset are advisory upper bounds, not completion events. A watch-first wake only shrinks action tokens: the host still supplies cached context. Removing the heartbeat can cold the cache; silent death can masquerade as no change.

**Q2.** Put adapters in C3 (B'). A browser-loaded catalogue conflicts with MV3: Chrome disables WebAssembly under the default extension CSP and requires `wasm-unsafe-eval` for the minimum enabling policy, while remotely fetched WASM is remote-hosted code ([CSP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/manifest/content-security-policy), [remote code](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/migrate/remote-hosted-code)).

Prefer native messaging to a loopback WebSocket: Chrome starts a bound native host and speaks stdio, with non-wildcard `allowed_origins` and port-scoped lifetime ([native messaging](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/native-messaging)). Minimal host API: verify catalogue/signature/revocation; begin a session bound to adapter hash, origin, tab, mode, capabilities and consent; draft composer; subscribe/read only the bound thread; explicit `send`; append audit; end session. Every bridge operation carries the per-run capability and refuses unmatched origin/tab.

**Q3.** Persist an interactive run record: `created`, `relay-connected`, `tab-bound`, `draft-written`, `awaiting-send`, `sent`, `streaming`, `parsing`, then exactly one terminal class: `completed`, `not-sent-expired`, `user-declined`, `tab-closed`, `relay-lost`, `extension-disconnected`, `abandoned-by-operator`, `partial-salvaged`, or `failed`. `awaiting-send` pauses stall/timeout and has its own consent expiry. Stop means record plus abandon/disconnect and partial salvage—never close the user’s tab. Do not seat draft-only browser reviewers in unattended detached runs or concurrent panels by default.

**Q4.** Omitted designs: the event journal; native messaging; a separate adapter-host process; an explicit cache-keepalive path; adapter rows keyed by content hash. To choose, measure host cache TTL/cached-input cost, actual silent-death rate, Chrome context/CSP behavior, native-messaging concurrency and service-worker lifetime, extension update controls, vendor autosave/terms, and user availability.
